page: Amazon Web Services a1.large is an ARM64-based server instance powered by the first-generation AWS Graviton processor. It features 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 vCPUs running at a clock speed of 2.3 GHz, utilizing the Cortex-A72 microarchitecture. The system is equipped with 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding 2.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and operates on a 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth under the Nitro hypervisor.

In benchmark evaluations, the a1.large demonstrates entry-level performance characteristics. Its single-core CPU performance via stress-ng falls within the average range at 1489.88, but multi-core performance is weak, scoring 2934.26. Memory bandwidth is a primary bottleneck, with read-only large block and write large block tests placing in the bottom 10% of results. Similarly, database operations, static web serving, and cryptographic operations score in the lowest tier, reflecting the limitations of the early ARMv8 architecture.

The instance lacks advanced vector extensions and virtualization flags, though it supports hardware-accelerated AES cryptography. Given the low memory bandwidth and weak multi-core scaling, this server is best positioned for lightweight, ARM-native development, basic containerized microservices, or low-traffic static web serving where high computational throughput is not required. It offers a qualitative cost-efficiency advantage for developers seeking a dedicated ARM64 environment without the overhead of high-performance x86 hardware.
